Describe the construct for an item-revision loop

Source: R/loop.R
loop_construct.Rd

loop_construct() holds what an item writer needs to know about the scale being built: The construct, its subscales, how many items to write and the response scale. revision_loop() passes it to the item writer and the reviser, and uses scale, labels and instructions to build the sc_instrument() that synthetic respondents answer.

Usage

loop_construct(
  name,
  definition = NULL,
  scales = NULL,
  n_per_scale = 6,
  reverse_share = 1/3,
  population = NULL,
  scale = c(1, 5),
  labels = NULL,
  instructions = sc_default_instructions,
  notes = NULL,
  criterion = NULL
)

Arguments

name

a short name for the construct, for example "Honesty-Humility".

definition

the definition of the construct, in a sentence or two.

scales

optional subscales: A named character vector, with the short names (used as scale in the item table) as names and their definitions as values. NULL makes one scale named after name.

n_per_scale

number of items to write for each scale.

reverse_share

share of reverse-keyed items to aim for.

population

who will answer the items, for example "adults in Canada".

scale, labels, instructions

the response scale, its labels and the instructions, as in sc_instrument().

notes

optional further guidance for the item writer and reviser, such as a style guide or a reading level.

criterion

optional stopping rule, a loop_criterion(), that revision_loop() uses for this construct unless it is given another.

Value

An object of class sc_construct_spec.

See also

revision_loop(), loop_builtin_construct()

Examples

loop_construct("Honesty-Humility",
               "Sincerity, fairness, greed avoidance and modesty.",
               scales = c(sincerity = "Not manipulating others for personal gain.",
                          fairness = "Not cheating or stealing."),
               n_per_scale = 4, scale = c(1, 5))
#> Construct "Honesty-Humility": 2 scales, 4 items each, answers 1 to 5.
#> Sincerity, fairness, greed avoidance and modesty. 
#>   sincerity: Not manipulating others for personal gain.
#>   fairness: Not cheating or stealing.
